page: Microsoft Azure D96alds_v6 is an x86_64 server instance within the Daldv6 series, powered by AMD processors running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 96 dedicated vCPUs alongside 192.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 2.0 GB memory-to-core allocation. The instance includes 5669 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage configurations. Hardware acceleration is not present, with zero physical or virtual GPUs allocated.

The hardware configuration trades standard memory density for high dedicated compute parallelism and massive high-speed local disk capacity. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides a compute-focused distribution rather than memory-heavy headroom. From a cost-efficiency perspective, bundling 5669 GB of high-speed local NVMe storage reduces reliance on separately billed external block storage volumes for scratch space, temporary indexing, and high-turnover local caching layers.

Without GPU acceleration or extensive memory buffers per core, workloads requiring deep memory residency or machine learning training are unsuited for this profile. Microsoft Azure D96alds_v6 is designed for compute-bound, multi-threaded tasks that demand fast, expansive local storage, including batch processing, continuous integration compilation tasks, distributed build pipelines, video transcode queues, and data processing engines with high scratch storage demands.
description: Microsoft Azure D96alds_v6 is an x86_64 server instance provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V, featuring 96 dedicated AMD vCPUs and 192.0 GB of system memory. Designed with a 2.0 GB per core ratio, this system departs from typical memory distributions in favor of dense CPU parallel processing paired with significant local storage capacity. It incorporates 5669 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and provides Premium Storage capability, while omitting GPU hardware and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The configuration offers strong resource density for disk-intensive batch pipelines, eliminating additional attachments for temporary high-throughput disk operations. The instance is suitable for CPU-bound distributed computation, software build clusters, high-capacity staging nodes, and batch analytics that process data across rapid local scratch disks without requiring elevated memory pools per core.
